Text S1 The specific parameters of liquid slurry reflux in the TSAD system.

The volume of the reflux liquid slurry is equal to that of the feed liquid of TR3 (e.g., under the total HRT of 30 days in the TSAD system, the reflux volume is 333.3 mL; under the total HRT of 20 days, the reflux volume is 500 mL; under the total HRT of 10 days, the reflux volume is 1000 mL). The reflux ratio, defined as the volumetric ratio of daily refluxed liquid slurry to daily distilled water addition, was maintained at approximately 3.7:1 to stabilize the TS concentration in TR1 at about 15%. Although the liquid slurry was refluxed, the solid residues needed to be regularly discharged from the system. According to mass balance, the net solid residue discharge mainly came from the solid phase retained after centrifugation of TR1, and the daily net solid discharge volumes of the three operational phases were calculated to be 150, 225, and 450 g/d respectively. In each operational phase, the purge ratio (the volumetric ratio of daily discharged solid residues to daily total feeding) was stably maintained at approximately 22.3%.

In the SSAD process, hydrolysis, acidification and methane production are carried out in the same reactor, and the carbon is ultimately distributed in the biogas residue, BS and CH4 and CO2. Calculations can be made according to Eq. (2) - (4).

In the TSAD process, hydrolysis, acidification and CH4 production are carried out in stages, and the carbon flow in each stage is calculated separately. The carbon in the hydrolysis stage is mainly distributed in the hydrolysis residue (CH,R, including the solid carbon after solid-liquid separation of the effluent from the hydrolysis stage, as well as the liquid carbon that did not enter the acidification stage, calculated according to Eq. (5)), the actual hydrolysate entering the acidification tank (CH,L→A), and the carbon lost in gaseous form under aerobic action (CLoss, Eq. (6)).

Where CH,S is the carbon of the solid fraction of the discharge from the hydrolysis stage; CH,L(total) is the total carbon of the liquid fraction of the discharge from the hydrolysis stage; CH,L→A is the liquid carbon that actually enters the acidification tank, calculated according to Eq. (2)-(3).

The acidification stage uses the hydrolyzed liquid as the feedstock, and the products include acidification solution and acidification gas (CH4 and CO2). The methanogenesis stage uses the acidified liquid as the feedstock, and the carbon is ultimately distributed in BS, CH4 and CO2. Calculations can be made according to Eq. (3) - (4). The pure inoculum treatment group serves as a blank control to subtract the background gas production of the inoculum.
